_meta.author: Aristotle
_meta.purpose: Bekker page -> treatise, for resolving Aristotelian citations. Because Bekker pagination is CONTINUOUS and globally unique across the corpus (1831 Berlin edition, pp. 1-1462), a bare number like 1094a self-identifies its treatise via this lookup. This is the easy sub-project.
_meta.edition_of_record: Bekker, Aristotelis Opera, Berlin 1831 (2 vols of Greek text, continuous pagination cols a/b)
_meta.format_note: Bekker cites look like 1094a1 or 980b25: 3-4 digit page + a/b column + optional line number. Format routing distinguishes from Stephanus (Aristotle = 4-digit-ish + a/b; Plato = 3-digit + a-e).
_meta.uniqueness_note: Unlike Stephanus, NO reset. Each page integer belongs to exactly one treatise. This table is therefore authoritative on its own; scope-tracking and abbreviation-matching are only needed to (a) catch OCR/tokenisation garble and (b) handle the boundary pages where two treatises share a page.
caveats: Pseudo-Aristotelian works ARE in the Bekker pagination (e.g. De Mundo, Problems, Magna Moralia disputed, De Coloribus, etc.) - included below, flagged authenticity where relevant. They still get cited.
Fragments use ROSE numbers, NOT Bekker - out of scope for this table; a Rose-numbered cite will not match any Bekker page and should route to a separate handler or the review queue.

The Athenaion Politeia (Constitution of the Athenians) is NOT in Bekker pagination (papyrus discovered 1879, post-Bekker) - cited by chapter/section, so it will not appear here and should be handled separately.
A handful of pages carry two treatises (one ends, next begins on same page). Boundary pages flagged VERIFY - the parser may need the abbreviation to break ties on exactly those pages.
_meta.VERIFY: All start/end pages verified:false. Check against a Bekker concordance (e.g. the page ranges in the Revised Oxford Translation, or Bekker 1831 directly). Boundary pages are approximate and are the likely error sites. Treatise ORDER follows the traditional Bekker sequence (Organon first, etc.).
